labels.label: BBS:l763:SO0=PSL
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right for 'groups only'. pslEquivLorentz : PSL(2,R) ≃* Causal.Flat.lorentz 2 is a real isomorphism. lorentz 2 is minkQ-preserving, future-cone-preserving and det 1, i.e. BBS's SO_0(1,2) of l.594-595. Checked by hand: spinL is X ↦ M X Mᵀ on X = [[t+x, y], [y, t−x]]. ker_spinLorentz gives spinLorentz.ker = center SL(2,R) through the faithful action on RP1, and a probe of my own derived spinLorentz g = 1 → g = 1 ∨ g = −1 and spinLorentz (−1) = 1 from it. It is onto because rotations (by half the angle) and boosts diag(e^{ζ/2}, e^{−ζ/2}) generate boostRot, and boostRot = ⊤ is strict (HSModel l.1003). PSL(2,R) is mathlib's SL ⧸ center. There is no topology on lorentz 2 at this pin (HSModel SCOPE (b)), so the Lie-group reading is honestly left as a question.

labels.label: BBS:l1903:bd=RP1
labels.notes: Unmarked, status closed, which holds for the planner's scope (1). rp1ToBdPlus : RP1 ≃ₜ HS.piece 2 .bdPlus is a real Homeomorph (circleToPenrose then bdPlusHomeomorph.symm). Its coordinate form w ↦ [(1, Re w, Im w)] and its spinor form mk z ↦ |z|⁻² S(z) are both proved. smul_rp1ToBdPlus says A • rp1ToBdPlus w = rp1ToBdPlus (pslEquivLorentz.symm A • w) for every A ∈ SO_0(1,2), and smul_rp1ToBdMinus is the same through the antipode. The paper itself defines ∂H²± as the boundaries of H²± in HS² (l.590), and the frontier is the strict GX.HS.frontier_hypPlus. So reading 'conformal boundary' as that frontier, and 'naturally' as 'equivariantly', is the model's content, not an extra reading. Uniqueness of the equivariant identification is true (PSL(2,R) has trivial centralizer in Homeo(RP1)) and is not claimed.

labels.label: BBS:l1903:hyperbolic-side
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right. IsPhoton is word for word l.1866-1867 over the maximal atlas. IsPhotonCircle (photons, relatively open in the photon set, homeomorphic to Circle) is no stronger than 'circle component of P' for Hausdorff M, so this reading does not narrow. The structure is a real (PSL(2,R), RP1)-structure: HasGroupoid C (gxGroupoid PSL(2,R) RP1) by photonChartOf_compatible, with chart changes pslEquivLorentz.symm of the SO_0(1,2) chart changes. It does not depend on the atlas: photonChartOf_mem_maximalAtlas puts the chart of every HS-chart of M's maximal atlas into C's maximal atlas. It is non-vacuous: my probe proved IsPhotonCircle (M := HS 2) (HS.piece 2 .bdPlus) in about ten lines, with standard axioms, and exists_hasLiftedHolonomy holds on it. Narrowing, disclosed (row partial, dispatch scope 'regular'): only circles in a non-singular HS-manifold. The paper's hyperbolic-side structure (l.1897-1905) is also defined for circles containing light-like singularities, which is not covered (finding 2). The structure comes from the charts, not from A_H's conformal boundary, and SCOPE (c) says so.

labels.label: BBS:l1907:isotropic-foliations
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right. HS² model only, disclosed in SCOPE (d). The leaves are the fibres of ι_ε over dS² and lie in the degenerate plane ⟨u, m⟩ with u null and u ⊥ m (leafPt_eq, minkB_leafNormal, minkQ_leafNormal). iotaChart gives a real (trivial) foliation. null_orth_cases with iotaL_ne_iotaR gives exactly two lightlike lines through each point of dS². By hand: the two dS²-arcs of u^⊥ are the L-leaf and the R-leaf over u, antipodal to each other, which matches nullDir_neg. Along the ε-leaf the spatial angle turns by −επ, as the REPORT says. 'Left' is a disclosed convention (ε = 1 makes (w, n_L) direct for vol3), and I checked vol3(e_x, e_t, n_1(e_x)) = 1 > 0. The checklist row uses '✓' where the content is model-only (finding 1).

labels.label: BBS:l2983:iota-L
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: right. This is the HS² form of a step in the proof of the ledger label bbslem:surgery_key (proof span l.2958-3011), not BBS's ι_L on d̃S² ∪ R₋ ∪ R₊; SCOPE (d) defers that to T-3p1-theorem-m-theta. The following are proved as stated: continuous_iota; isProperMap_iota (trivial here, since closedDS is compact; in d̃S² it is not); iota_smul (SO_0(1,2)-equivariant); iotaChart (closedDS ≃ₜ ∂H²₊ × [−1,1]); closure_leafOver (closure = leaf ∪ {u, −u}); existsUnique_alpha and existsUnique_omega; identity on ∂H²₊ and antipode on ∂H²₋ for both ε. The latter backs the REPORT's note that ι_L = ι_R on ∂H²₋ in HS². iota_rp1ToBdMinus ('projective on ∂H²₋') is tautological by the choice rp1ToBdMinus = −rp1ToBdPlus, but true. 'Submersion' is read topologically. The REPORT discloses this; the docstring only implies it through iotaChart.

findings.what: The finding that the left isotropic foliation is never defined is accurate: 'left' appears only at l.2983 and l.2989, and § 6.3 names F₁, F₂ with no assignment. It is not a false finding. But the paper does fix a 'left'/'right' convention, for the two families of lines ruling the boundary quadric Q of AdS₃ (L_l, L_r, l.402-404). Through the link L(p) ≅ HS² of the suspension, each isotropic leaf through v spans with p a lightlike plane tangent to Q. That plane meets Q in one left and one right line, and the ray of v ends on one of them. This is a plausible source of the paper's 'left' (my own reading, not checked in Lean). The question offers only the orientation convention.
findings.fix: In the question to the author, offer the l.402-404 ruling convention as a second candidate beside the vol3 orientation convention.
